rename.from: Microsoft Office apps can't write on an S3 mount when mounted with nfsmount
rename.to: Microsoft Office apps can't write on an S3 mount when mounted with nfsmount on MacOS 14.5

body: Remove MacFUSE (if you have it), install [FUSE-T](https://www.fuse-t.org/) (available via brew) and use `rclone mount`. It is kext-less and under the hood it uses nfs, the same as `rclone nfsmount` but from my experience is more stable and compliant (it uses macOS nfs server and not some home brewed implementation). At least for me no problem with opening and writing MS Office docs.

@ncw , @kapitainsky , OK, so I tested on the Intel computer that I have here for testing, and I tested on a an empty S3 folder so the log file is hopefully easier to read for you. Something weird happened while testing this time.  Here is what happened...

1) I created a new file "test.docx" in MS Word, and tried to save it to S3. It looked like it is saving it, I got a spinning ball for about 20-30 seconds, and it seemed like it has been saved, but Word crashed. 
2) I reopened Word and tried to open the file from the drive, and it opened, but in read only mode. Also, the file didn't have the text that I wrote in it, it was blank. I tried to edit the file, but couldn't because Word said that it was read only.
3) I created a new file "test 2.docx" and tried to save it to the the drive again. Again the same thing happened, it initially saved the file after a while, but then Word switched to read only mode, and there was no content in it, it was empty.

Here is the log file from all of this:
[Terminal Saved Output.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/16433963/Terminal.Saved.Output.txt)

When I finished the session and unmounted the drive, I went to the S3 console from my browser and downloaded the two files just to see what was written. They are 0 (zero) kilobytes in size, and they have no content, they are completely blank. Very weird what happens.

@alexbet I think Word crashing is why the file ended up empty.

So we need to work out why Word crashed.

There are no errors or anything unusual in the log you provided.

Are there any errors in the macOS kernel logs? That is probably where NFS errors end up.

BTW I merged those NFS fixes into [the latest beta](https://beta.rclone.org/) now.
